industryStateSource.interpretation: High expansion with long delivery and high input prices, but slowing new-order/backlog momentum and rising inventory.

bridgeRules: A broad Taiwan electronics/optical PMI state may be attached as industry context only when issuer product scope is independently evidenced.
Formal TWSE industry taxonomy and PMI survey category are different classification systems; category membership must not be assumed one-to-one.
Revenue exposure weight remains UNKNOWN unless the issuer discloses a compatible revenue/product denominator.
Survey membership is UNKNOWN unless explicitly disclosed; do not claim the issuer contributed to the PMI survey.
Industry backlog/lead-time state cannot be converted into issuer backlog, revenue growth, margin or stock score without issuer-native evidence.
negativeControls: 8046 and 3189 sit in different TWSE formal industries despite both having IC-substrate exposure; this falsifies a one-taxonomy theme mapping.
The same broad electronics PMI state can affect substrate makers differently by customer mix, node/product mix, qualification, utilization, pricing terms and inventory.
High supplier-delivery time can coexist with slowing new-order momentum and high inventory, so a direct positive company score is prohibited.
reasonNoPromotion: Product-scope bridging is PIT-feasible, but revenue magnitude, survey membership and issuer-native order/backlog clocks remain incomplete; no company-level predictive efficacy is established.
exactNext: SC-042 define the shortage/supply-gap event contract with independent evidence for demand, constrained supply, allocation/lead-time, price and inventory state.
For future issuer mapping, add disclosed product/revenue exposure weights before using industry states in any System1/System2 research score.
Keep issuer order/backlog and stock outcomes closed until native company disclosures are captured on their own publication clocks.
